$comment: The one definition of a knowledge note: its fields, its fixed sections, the node and relationship vocabulary and what the check enforces. Read by scripts/knowledge-structure/ (the check, the index and the skeleton). Nothing else restates it. Why: decision 0022. How to write a note: note-template.md.

limits.noteLinesCount: lines below the front matter, blank lines included

fields.what: The short name the index and the map show.
What the note describes: one of noteTypes, which is also a node type.
One line, in plain words, of what the part is for. The index line is made from it.
Other names a reader may search for (a list; empty when there are none).

Only what the code and the generated reference cannot show: a list of { type, target }, type from relationshipTypes with hand set to true, target a path in the repository (a list; empty when there are none).

noteTypes.module: A business area under src/modules/ with its own screens, rules and data.
noteTypes.platform-area: Shared code under src/platform/ that modules and pages build on.
noteTypes.feature: One piece with its own logic spread over several files, inside a module or a platform area.

sections.heading: Screens
sections.hint: Only for a module with routes: one line each on where its data comes from. The routes themselves are in docs/reference/routes.md: link it, do not copy it.

sections.heading: How the pieces link
sections.hint: How its fields, flags, hooks and files connect and depend on each other and on other notes, where the code does not show it at a glance.

sections.heading: Behaviors and events
sections.hint: What happens that the config does not show: hooks, jobs, emails, cache tags, time windows, limits. One line each, with the file.

sections.heading: Shared pieces it uses
sections.hint: Components, helpers and blocks from src/platform/, one line each. Where it meets another module, name the composition root that joins them (decision 0008).

sections.heading: Rules and the tests that protect them
sections.hint: Each business rule in a sentence, with its test.

sections.heading: Boundaries
sections.hint: What it may import, what imports it, what it must never do.

sections.heading: Decisions
sections.hint: Links to the decision records and issues that explain why it is this way.

sections.heading: Known gaps
sections.hint: Open issues and limits to know before changing it: the node's watch-outs on the map. Write None when there are none.

feature.what: One piece with its own logic, inside a module or area.

screen.what: A page route a visitor opens.

endpoint.what: An HTTP address that answers with data, not a page.

mcp-tool.what: A tool an AI agent calls through the MCP address.

collection.what: A CMS content type with many documents.

global.what: A CMS content type with one document.

block.what: A page-builder or rich-text block an editor places.

shared-component.what: A component of the UI kit or rich text.

job.what: Work the app runs on its own schedule or queue.

scheduled-task.what: A task that runs by the clock outside the app.

note.what: A knowledge note next to the code it describes.

workflow-step.what: One step of how a change is made.

check.what: A mechanical gate: a required check or a script.

contains.derivedFrom: folders and the screens and content-type references

writes.derivedFrom: the content-type reference and the code

calls.derivedFrom: the routes reference and the code

depends-on.derivedFrom: written only when no import or reference shows it

owned-by.derivedFrom: written: which role owns the subject

NOTE-FRONTMATTER.what: A note starts with a front matter block that parses.

NOTE-FIELDS.what: The fields are exactly those of fields, in that order.

NOTE-FIELD-VALUE.what: Each field has the right shape: one-line summary within the limit, lists of the right items.

NOTE-TYPE.what: The type is one of noteTypes.

NOTE-RELATIONSHIP.what: Each relationship has a type from relationshipTypes that may be written by hand.

NOTE-RELATIONSHIP-TARGET.what: Each relationship target is a path that exists.

NOTE-TITLE.what: A level 1 title, then a purpose paragraph, before the first section.

NOTE-SECTIONS.what: Level 2 headings are those of sections for the type, in order, once each, and every required one is there.

NOTE-PATH.what: Every backticked path and every file link in a note exists.

NOTE-ORPHAN.what: Every README under notes.discover is a map entry's note.

MAP-NOTE.what: Every map entry names a note that exists, once.

NOTE-NO-CODE.what: A note's map paths match code, and the note names code.

INDEX-DRIFT.what: The index lists each map note, in map order, with the line made from its name and summary.

COVERAGE-SECTION.what: A section marked expected is missing (becomes blocking in #1004).

COVERAGE-CODE.what: Source code that no map entry describes (becomes blocking in #1004).
